zen.text: The Eldrazi were still only a half-forgotten legend in Zendikar's first story, as Ayli remarked beside their monument that gods do not die, they merely slumber.

Nahiri had built the network of hedrons over forty years to imprison them, with Ugin guiding her, and when cultists in Akoum later loosened the prison with their rituals, broods sprang into existence and devastated the plane.

Zendikar's angels tried to resist, but were defeated and wore their halos over their eyes; the kor empire fell and most of the Mul Daya were wiped out, while elementals rose from the plane itself like antibodies against the invaders.
Within two years of the Eldrazi's release, the continents of Bala Ged and Sejiri were overrun and destroyed, and survivors like the kor gathered around Glasspool to carve dwellings into the peaks.

roe.text: Thousands of years earlier, three Eldrazi had descended on Zendikar and spawned brood lineages to pillage it, until Ugin, a lithomancer and Sorin Markov trapped them there with a lock-spell at the Eye of Ugin.

The three planeswalkers had meant to rid the Multiverse of the Eldrazi but could not defeat them, so Sorin lured them in, Ugin bound them with colorless magic and Nahiri built the hedron prison, and Zendikar slowly recovered as the broods died off and the colossi fell inert.

Later, vampires built a shrine that destabilized the prison, and Nahiri woke and restored it alone, but when Sorin returned with Nissa, she shattered the main hedron at the Eye of Ugin and released the titans.

The Eldrazi rose again and the hedrons coalesced into colossal superstructures, each titan spawning a brood lineage around it, and people were soon being snuffed out where they stood; Sea Gate and the Enclave fell, and Noyan Dar led refugees upriver to found Coralhelm Refuge.

m11.text: When the Eldrazi arose once more on Zendikar, the merfolk realized that they had mistaken the Eldrazi's names for legends of gods.

ori.text: A thousand years before the great reawakening, the Eldrazi stirred and Nahiri woke from her long slumber, sensing that the prison had been opened.
She buried the broods she found beneath avalanches and decided she must stop them alone, then reshaped a statue into a new hedron, repaired the network and drove the titans back into torpor.

In the later fighting Gideon killed a monstrosity with a hedron shard and held a canyon pass against spawn so that survivors from Bala Ged could escape, before a great host descended on Sea Gate and overwhelmed it.
Elsewhere, Jace admitted to himself that he had inadvertently released them from millennia of imprisonment, and Nissa and Ashaya fought small groups of them, though one consumed a kor's life.

bfz.text: Nahiri, Ugin and Sorin Markov had used hedrons to trap the Eldrazi, but thousands of years later Sarkhan, Chandra and Jace met in the Eye of Ugin chamber and unintentionally loosened their bonds, and Nissa broke the last of them, thinking they would leave Zendikar behind.
She was wrong: Eldrazi of Ulamog's lineage ravaged Bala Ged, and within two years Sea Gate, Sejiri and Bala Ged were overrun.

Gideon and Jace found Sea Gate overrun and held off the Eldrazi so survivors could flee, while Nissa and Ashaya rescued refugees at Fartree Hamlet and Iona descended from Emeria to fight, though her power could not fend off the titans' colorless magic.

Gideon then gathered Drana, Noyan Dar, Tazri, Nissa and Kiora's forces, and together they wrested Sea Gate away from the Eldrazi, as Noyan unleashed the Roil to collapse the ground and kill the horde.

jmp.text: Ugin told Jace that the Eldrazi can be imprisoned by hedrons, and Jace doubted it, asking how that had worked out last time.

j22.text: Ugin again told Jace that the Eldrazi could be imprisoned by hedrons, and Jace stayed skeptical after how it had gone last time.

fdn.text: Even after the Eldrazi died, the Roil did not stop, though its death should have stilled it.
